standard: The Self (docs/enrichment/dossiers/the-self.md) and Anger (anger.md) are the exemplars: exhaustive map (every wiki card on the theme, grouped by subtheme), real divergences with verbatim-checked quotes from opened carriers, Variation-Selection(+Retention) practice section, Nearby terms section per DISAMBIGUATION.md.
deliverables: docs/enrichment/sources/dossiers/<slug>.md (evidence ledger, every quote verified word-for-word against an opened carrier)
registry status flip to published is SUPERVISOR-ONLY: leave status 'planned' and flag in a commit message
the Academy data splice is SUPERVISOR-ONLY: do NOT edit site/assets/app.js or style.css; never edit registry.json, progress.json or the queues
verification: Every card link verified against actual content/ filenames by script before pushing. No hallucination: every fact and quote from a source actually opened (owner library: docs/PRIMARY-SOURCES.md). Humanised per HUMANIZER-SKILL.md.

baton: python3 scripts/baton.py clock-in <band> <agent-name>; clock in at every milestone; release when the band's list is exhausted.

concepts: Extended process model of emotion regulation
Process model of emotion regulation Gross
principles: A042 — Recognise that virtue is a hexis, not a feeling
A114 — Understand that emotions are cognitive
A122 — Recognise that emotions shape judgment
AF001 — Treat affect as information, not as verdict
AF002 — Distinguish the feeling from its interpretation
AF003 — Learn the structure of your affect — valence and arousal
AF004 — Cultivate emotional granularity — name feelings precisely
AF006 — Accept mixed feelings; do not force them to resolve
AF007 — Recognise affective forecasting errors; expect hedonic adaptation
AF009 — Understand that affect is constructed, not discovered
AF010 — Recognise that affect has temporal structure — intensity, duration, variability, recovery
AF011 — Know that affect has a biological substrate; do not moralise it
AF012 — Recognise that affect is socially and culturally shaped; do not universalise it
AF013 — Train emotional recovery — the ability to return to baseline
AF014 — Recognise emotional inertia — the difference between feeling and getting stuck
AF015 — Do not fear emotional variability; fear its absence
AF016 — Cultivate emodiversity — the range and evenness of your emotional life
AF017 — Recognise that positive and negative affect are not opposite ends of one axis
AF018 — Understand that affect is regulated by reward prediction error, not by outcomes alone
AF019 — Recognise the paradox of hedonic pursuit — chasing positive affect can reduce it
AF021 — Understand affective presence — your feelings influence others' feelings
AF022 — Recognise affective contagion in groups; do not mistake it for your own feeling
AF023 — Know that affect changes memory; do not trust emotional memory as a record
AF024 — Recognise affect's relationship to motivation; use it, do not obey it
AF028 — Master emotional regulation flexibility — the skill is matching strategy to context
AF034 — Cultivate equanimity — the capacity to remain steady amid affect
AF036 — Learn to regulate through action — affect follows behaviour
AF039 — Learn acceptance — the willingness to have a feeling without fighting it
AF040 — Distinguish accepting a feeling from accepting a circumstance
AF041 — Learn distress tolerance — the capacity to bear intense affect without making it worse
AF042 — Practise opposite action — do the opposite of what the feeling urges
AF043 — Learn to observe feelings without identification — you are not your affect
AF044 — Recognise secondary emotions — feelings about feelings
AF045 — Learn to let affect pass — feelings are impermanent
AF061 — Cultivate positive affect deliberately — it broadens and builds
AF072 — Recognise that positive affect alone is not flourishing; it is one component
AF073 — Learn co-regulation — affect is regulated with others, not just within
AF075 — Learn emotional validation — acknowledging a feeling reduces its intensity
AF077 — Learn emotional disclosure — the capacity to share feelings in a way that helps
AF078 — Recognise when affect requires professional help — clinical boundaries
sayings: Beware the moods of the many
